reviews.author: Radhe Krishna Shaw
reviews.originalText:
The temple is truly one of the most breathtaking landmarks in Penang and a must visit destination for anyone exploring the island. As one of the largest and most important Buddhist temples in Southeast Asia, it offers a remarkable blend of spirituality, culture, history, and stunning architecture.From the moment you enter the temple complex, you are greeted by beautifully decorated prayer halls, intricate carvings, colorful pagodas, and peaceful gardens. Every corner showcases impressive craftsmanship and centuries of cultural heritage. The iconic Pagoda of Ten Thousand Buddhas and the towering statue of the Goddess of Mercy, Guan Yin, are particularly magnificent and worth the visit alone.What impressed me most was the serene atmosphere despite the popularity of the site. Walking through the temple grounds felt peaceful and calming, allowing plenty of time for reflection while appreciating the beautiful surroundings. The elevated location also offers spectacular panoramic views of Penang, making it a fantastic spot for photography.

The temple is well maintained, and there is plenty to explore, so allow enough time to fully experience the complex. Whether you are interested in religion, architecture, history, or simply looking for one of Penang’s most iconic attractions, Kek Lok Si Temple delivers an unforgettable experience.

A truly inspiring and beautiful place that should not be missed when visiting Penang.

reviews.author: Chng Zi Long
reviews.originalText:
One of the most famous spots in Penang. It has been renovated extensively, with many new buildings added since I was young. The temple's signature feature is the massive Guan Yin statue, which is roughly 30 meters tall.

​In addition to the main statue, there are many other deities and intricate carvings inside the temple, and it takes quite a while to explore them all. Even though I was just roaming around and sightseeing, I easily spent about two hours there. My favorite part was the large, gorgeous mural (or wall carvings) on the upper level of one of the temple buildings.

​Since the temple is built on a mountainside, you can also get a fantastic view of Penang city, making it a perfect spot for photography.

reviews.author: G&Ts World
reviews.originalText:
Kek Lok Si Temple is one of Penang’s most impressive cultural attractions and an experience that should not be rushed.

The temple complex is much larger than we expected, with beautifully detailed architecture, colourful prayer halls, landscaped gardens, statues and peaceful spaces to explore. Every level revealed something different, and the elevated location provided impressive views across Air Itam and George Town.

The towering bronze statue of the Goddess of Mercy, Kuan Yin, is an extraordinary sight, while the Pagoda of Ten Thousand Buddhas was another highlight. The combination of Chinese, Thai and Burmese architectural influences makes the temple unique and provides plenty of opportunities for photography and quiet reflection.

Entry to much of the complex is free, although small fees apply to access some areas and use the lifts. Allow at least two to three hours if you want to explore properly rather than simply visit the main viewpoints.

The temple involves stairs, slopes and walking between different levels, so comfortable footwear is recommended. Dress respectfully, carry water and visit earlier in the day if you want to avoid some of the heat and larger crowds.

A beautiful and culturally significant place that showcases Penang’s history, spirituality and architectural diversity. One of the highlights of our time in Penang and an essential addition to any itinerary.

Greg&Trina.

reviews.author: Sercan Çelik
reviews.originalText:
Kek Lok Si Temple is one of the most impressive and beautiful temples in Malaysia and is undoubtedly one of the highlights of visiting Penang. As the largest Buddhist temple in the country, it combines stunning architecture, peaceful gardens, and breathtaking views over George Town.

The temple complex is enormous, with countless halls, prayer areas, pagodas, and beautifully decorated buildings to explore. One of the main highlights is the magnificent Pagoda of Ten Thousand Buddhas, which blends Chinese, Thai, and Burmese architectural styles. The towering statue of the Goddess of Mercy (Kuan Yin) is equally impressive and offers spectacular panoramic views of the surrounding area.

Walking through the temple is a peaceful experience. The colorful lanterns, intricate carvings, and beautifully maintained gardens create a calm and spiritual atmosphere. Every corner reveals something new, making it easy to spend several hours exploring the complex.

The temple is also an excellent place for photography, especially in the early morning or late afternoon when the lighting enhances the beauty of the buildings. Despite being a popular attraction, the large grounds ensure there are many quiet spots to appreciate the scenery.

Overall, Kek Lok Si Temple is an absolute must-visit in Penang. Whether you're interested in history, architecture, Buddhism, or simply looking for one of the island's most beautiful landmarks, this temple offers an unforgettable experience and is well worth the visit.

reviews.author: Dato' Paduka Panji Utara
reviews.originalText:
Experience at BOH Sungai Palas Tea Centre, Cameron Highlands
Spending time at BOH Sungai Palas Tea Centre with my beloved wife was one of the most memorable moments of our trip to Cameron Highlands. The breathtaking scenery of the endless green tea fields, cool mountain breeze, and peaceful atmosphere made it the perfect place to relax and unwind.
We enjoyed a delicious lunch at the tea restaurant, including a warm bowl of soto, a hot cup of freshly brewed BOH tea, and a delightful strawberry cheesecake. Everything tasted even better while overlooking the beautiful tea plantation.
After our meal, we took a leisurely walk around the tea fields, admired the spectacular views, and captured many beautiful photos together. It was a wonderful experience filled with nature, good food, and precious memories.
A highly recommended destination for anyone visiting Cameron Highlands. We will definitely be back again!

reviews.originalText:
I had an amazing experience at Sunway Lagoon and it truly deserves a 5-star rating. This is definitely one of the best theme parks in Malaysia for families, friends, couples, and even solo visitors looking for a fun and exciting day out. The park is huge and offers so many attractions that there is something for everyone to enjoy.

The water park was one of my favourite sections. The slides were thrilling, the wave pool was fun, and the overall environment felt clean and well-maintained. I also enjoyed the amusement park rides, especially the more adventurous ones that gave an adrenaline rush. The wildlife park and scream park added even more variety to the experience, making the whole visit feel complete and worth the ticket price.

What impressed me most was how organised and lively the park was. Despite the large crowd, the staff members were friendly, helpful, and professional. The facilities such as restrooms, lockers, and dining areas were also conveniently located and generally well-kept. There were plenty of food options available, so it was easy to spend the entire day there comfortably.

The atmosphere throughout the park was energetic, vibrant, and full of excitement. Every corner had something interesting to see or try. It is truly a place where unforgettable memories can be created with loved ones. I would highly recommend Sunway Lagoon to both locals and tourists visiting Malaysia. I will definitely visit again in the future.

Sunway Lagoon is a fantastic destination for families and offers a full day of fun for all ages. Surprisingly, even on a Saturday, the park wasn’t too crowded, so we managed to enjoy almost every ride without having to wait in long queues. We bought the family ticket using klook and get discount using maybank credit card

The park is huge, and getting around is convenient thanks to the train service that connects different areas. We also enjoyed the bird show, which was entertaining and especially great for kids.

Among all the attractions, The Storm was definitely the highlight of the day—an exhilarating ride that’s a must-try for thrill seekers!

Overall, Sunway Lagoon is a well-maintained theme park with a great variety of attractions, making it an excellent choice for a family outing.

reviews.author: SANKER P S
reviews.originalText:
We visited Sunway Lagoon recently as part of our Malaysia family trip and arrived right at 9:00 AM to make the most of the day. Overall, it was a great experience!

​The water park was a highlight—the splash pools and wave pools were excellent. My son particularly loved the FlowRider, which was a huge hit! We also enjoyed the adrenaline of the various water rides and the views from the Suspension Bridge.

​What makes this place unique is the variety. Beyond the water rides, the Wildlife Park (birds, snakes, and other animals) was amazing and well worth the time. On the downside, the horror show was just 'okay' and didn't quite live up to the hype.

​Comparison: If you are coming from India and are used to the high-thrill rides at Wonderla, you might find the specific ride intensity here slightly lower. However, when you combine the water park, the animal encounters, and the overall atmosphere, it is a very complete package. Definitely worth a visit! 4/5 stars.

There was a zoo, water park and dry theme park all in one. We enjoyed feeding the animals at the zoo where the multi feed packs are affordable starting from RM15. Highly recommended for families and young adult friends to visit.

reviews.originalText:
I had an amazing experience at Sunway Lagoon and it truly deserves a 5-star rating. This is definitely one of the best theme parks in Malaysia for families, friends, couples, and even solo visitors looking for a fun and exciting day out. The park is huge and offers so many attractions that there is something for everyone to enjoy.

The water park was one of my favourite sections. The slides were thrilling, the wave pool was fun, and the overall environment felt clean and well-maintained. I also enjoyed the amusement park rides, especially the more adventurous ones that gave an adrenaline rush. The wildlife park and scream park added even more variety to the experience, making the whole visit feel complete and worth the ticket price.

What impressed me most was how organised and lively the park was. Despite the large crowd, the staff members were friendly, helpful, and professional. The facilities such as restrooms, lockers, and dining areas were also conveniently located and generally well-kept. There were plenty of food options available, so it was easy to spend the entire day there comfortably.

The atmosphere throughout the park was energetic, vibrant, and full of excitement. Every corner had something interesting to see or try. It is truly a place where unforgettable memories can be created with loved ones. I would highly recommend Sunway Lagoon to both locals and tourists visiting Malaysia. I will definitely visit again in the future.

reviews.originalText:
📍Pantai Kemayang, Kelantan
This is perhaps my FAVOURITE beach of all time in Kota Bharu.
The amazing view, the chill vibes with the breeze, and the simple but incredibly delicious food; it was perfect.

This beach is a lagoon surrounded by man-made surf breakers - rocks extending far out to the horizon. We walked on these rocks to the very end. It was most breezy and extremely picturesque.

What I also thoroughly enjoyed was the food! Keropok Lekor, coconut juice, Ais Jagung and the best of all was Maggi Kari served Kelantan-style. The Maggi Kari was so incredible that I actually have cravings for it till today; it had limau nipis, the broth was thicker, and there were more spices.

With my limited time in Kota Bharu, this beach definitely tops my list. Hopefully, I'll be able to visit Kelantan again with Michelle if time permits. 2 days wasn't enough to explore this beautiful place.

reviews.author: Dajana
reviews.originalText:
As of May 2026 there is nothing to see anymore. All the coral is dead. There is some fish, but you can see the same fish in the ocean anywhere around Redang.
It's very sad, because the Marine park charges MYR30/pax conservation FEE but they aren't taking care of the place. The tourists (and locals alike) leave so much trash behind, step on the corals and use sunscreen when going to the water. This has caused the corals to die out in the recent years.

I visited Redang Island about 6years ago and there were still colorful corals to be seen, especially on Long Beach. This has changed so much , and it is sad. At least if the locals would take care of the island, but they leave the trash everywhere. It became very dirty.

(Pictures are from Long Beach)

reviews.author: Ilaria Mariani
reviews.originalText:
We had such a beautiful experience at the Marine Park! Right under the dock we saw huge schools of fish swimming all together—such an incredible sight! And we could swim among them!! There were also various corals, a nursery of baby corals, and many other kinds of fish. The highlight was spotting a shark (not too close, not so big, so no worries!).

We found it super useful to have life jackets, which allowed us to swim for almost two hours without worrying about getting tired. A good mask is essential to enjoy all the details underwater, and we also recommend wearing a UV/UVB protection shirt to avoid sunburn.

Absolutely worth the visit—stunning marine life and an unforgettable snorkeling experience!

reviews.author: Prince of the Earth
reviews.originalText: A fantastic addition to our Malaysia trip! The Marine Park offers stunningly clear waters and an abundance of beautiful marine life. It’s incredibly well-preserved and provided a safe, unforgettable snorkeling experience for the whole family. Watching the kids get so excited about seeing the underwater world up close was a definite highlight. Highly recommended if you are in the Terengganu area!

reviews.originalText:
We had complimentary access to the water park as part of our stay at Hard Rock Hotel Desaru Coast.

The park is fairly large with a good mix of attractions for both children and adults. There are plenty of water slides, a wave pool, lazy river, and dedicated play areas for younger kids. We especially liked that there was enough variety to keep everyone occupied for most of the day.

One convenient feature is that hotel guests with eligible access can enter and exit the park multiple times throughout the day. This made it easy to head back to the hotel room for a rest, meal, or shower before returning later.

The park was generally well maintained, and there were plenty of lifeguards around which added some reassurance, especially for families with young children. There are also lockers, food outlets, and shaded areas available throughout the park.

Overall, we had an enjoyable time. It may not be the biggest water park around, but it's a fun family-friendly attraction with a good range of rides and facilities. If you're staying at Hard Rock and have complimentary access included, it's definitely worth making full use of it.

Although it's not as large as Sunway Lagoon, it's definitely a great spot for a one-day getaway with the kids.
Since it was a long weekend combined with a public holiday, the park was quite crowded, which was understandable. Unfortunately, we didn't get the chance to try most of the rides due to the long queues. Even buying food required a considerable wait.
The weather was a bit unpredictable, with intermittent rain throughout the day. As a result, many visitors were looking for shelter, but there weren't many covered areas available apart from the surau.
On a positive note, the parking area was spacious. However, after a thunderstorm, the parking payment machines experienced technical issues, and visitors were allowed to exit without making payment. I'm still unsure whether this will affect my Touch 'n Go card.
Overall, it was an enjoyable experience and a nice place for a family day trip. Despite the crowds and weather, it's still worth visiting for a fun day out with the children.

reviews.author: Melvin J.
reviews.originalText:
We had complimentary access to the water park as part of our stay at Hard Rock Hotel Desaru Coast.

The park is fairly large with a good mix of attractions for both children and adults. There are plenty of water slides, a wave pool, lazy river, and dedicated play areas for younger kids. We especially liked that there was enough variety to keep everyone occupied for most of the day.

One convenient feature is that hotel guests with eligible access can enter and exit the park multiple times throughout the day. This made it easy to head back to the hotel room for a rest, meal, or shower before returning later.

The park was generally well maintained, and there were plenty of lifeguards around which added some reassurance, especially for families with young children. There are also lockers, food outlets, and shaded areas available throughout the park.

Overall, we had an enjoyable time. It may not be the biggest water park around, but it's a fun family-friendly attraction with a good range of rides and facilities. If you're staying at Hard Rock and have complimentary access included, it's definitely worth making full use of it.

reviews.author: Athira Azali
reviews.originalText: Got the water park voucher because I bought the Hard Rock Hotel voucher. Nothing much to complain about — for me, it was okay. As long as the kids were having fun, I was fine with it. However, there weren’t that many attractions in the water park. By around 2 p.m., we had already gone on all the rides, and the kids didn’t really know what else to do. If you’re buying separate tickets, I’d say it’s quite overpriced.

reviews.author: Mohd Razlan Jaafar
reviews.originalText:
Fantastic and hassle-free family day out! ⭐⭐⭐⭐

We had an absolutely wonderful time visiting with my wife and two kids. Booking our tickets online beforehand was a great decision. When we arrived, we just showed the digital tickets at the counter and entered in less than 10 minutes. There was no queue at all, making the process incredibly fast and smooth.

The entire place is highly kids-friendly. Because of the excellent setup, we spent our whole time at the dedicated kids' area, which kept the children completely entertained. Even though the weather wasn't ideal—with a light rain falling from the morning until we finished around 3:00 PM—it didn't dampen our spirits or ruin our fun at all.

Overall, it was a fantastic experience despite the rainy weather. We highly recommend this place to other families and will definitely be coming back for a second visit!

reviews.author: Peng Wan Choo
reviews.originalText: Fun destination for families, and it's super convenient if you're staying at Hard Rock Hotel as it’s just a short walk away via a dedicated entrance. The park has a good mix of slides and pools, making it enjoyable for both kids and adults. However, during our visit, the artificial wave pool was not operational, which was a bit disappointing. That said, the other rides and lazy river were still entertaining, and the park was clean and well-managed.

reviews.author: John (John)
reviews.originalText:
⭐ Petronas Twin Towers — An Icon of Kuala Lumpur

One of the most impressive landmarks in Kuala Lumpur and definitely a place worth visiting, especially for a first trip to Malaysia. The Petronas Twin Towers are instantly recognizable and give you that “I’m really in KL” feeling as soon as you see them.

The towers are especially beautiful from the outside. Their silver architectural design reflects the sunlight during the day and becomes even more impressive when illuminated at night. The area around KLCC is also well maintained, with open spaces, greenery, shopping, restaurants, and plenty of places to sit and enjoy the view.

📸 Best part: Walk around the surrounding park and find different angles for photos. The towers look very different depending on where you stand.

🌙 My recommendation: Visit both during the day and after sunset. The daytime view shows the architecture clearly, while the nighttime view gives the towers a completely different atmosphere.

For travelers, this is more than just a photo spot—it's one of those landmarks that represents the modern identity of Kuala Lumpur.

A must-visit landmark in KL. If you're in Kuala Lumpur and haven't seen the Twin Towers yet, definitely put it on your list! 🇲🇾✨

reviews.author: Santhosh Raj
reviews.originalText:
Visiting the Petronas Twin Towers was undoubtedly one of the highlights of my trip to Kuala Lumpur. The towers are even more breathtaking in person than in photographs, and seeing them transform from gleaming silver in the afternoon sunlight to beautifully illuminated at night was truly unforgettable.

The entire visit was exceptionally well organized. Entry was managed in small groups with dedicated time slots for the Skybridge and Observation Deck, making the experience comfortable without feeling overcrowded. The panoramic views of Kuala Lumpur from the top are absolutely spectacular and well worth the visit. I also enjoyed learning about the history, engineering, and architecture of this iconic landmark.

The café on Level 86 is a wonderful place to take a short break, enjoy a drink, and admire the stunning skyline before heading back down.

The area surrounding the towers is just as impressive, with the beautifully maintained KLCC Park and fountains providing plenty of space to relax and capture amazing photos from different angles.

Whether you admire architecture, enjoy city viewpoints, or simply want to experience one of Malaysia’s most iconic landmarks, the Petronas Twin Towers are an absolute must-visit. I highly recommend booking your tickets in advance to avoid disappointment.

reviews.author: vaasugi batumalai
reviews.originalText:
Visited over the weekend and had a great experience at the Skybridge, Twin Towers. We had already purchased our tickets via Klook, which made the entry process smooth and hassle-free.

The visit started at Level 41, where the Skybridge is located. The viewing time here was limited to about 10 minutes, but it was enough to take in the stunning city views and snap some nice photos. After that, we were guided to Level 86 for another 10 minutes, offering an even more breathtaking panoramic view of Kuala Lumpur.

We also stopped by Level 83, which had displays filled with interesting information, souvenirs, and exhibits. It added a nice touch to the overall experience.

Before leaving, we picked up a fridge magnet for RM16.50 as a memory of the visit. Overall, we truly enjoyed the views, the photo opportunities, and the well-organized flow of the tour. Afterward, we spent time at Suria KLCC for a meal and some shopping, which made the day even more enjoyable.

A great experience and definitely worth visiting at least once!

reviews.author: veeraphong jiraphanphong
reviews.originalText:
The Petronas Twin Towers is definitely a must visit landmark if you come to Malaysia. The iconic towers offer an unforgettable experience, especially when you visit the Skybridge on the 41st floor, where you can enjoy a beautiful view of Kuala Lumpur and appreciate the impressive architecture of the towers.

If you go higher up to the observation deck on the 86th floor, the experience becomes even more spectacular. The panoramic 360-degree view of Kuala Lumpur is truly breathtaking, offering an amazing perspective of the city and its surrounding skyline.

After your visit to the towers, you can explore the shopping mall at the lower levels, which offers a wide variety of shops, including fashion, cosmetics, perfumes, lifestyle brands, restaurants, and cafés. It is also a great place to relax, have a coffee, or enjoy a meal after sightseeing.

I highly recommend visiting in the morning, around 10:00 a.m., when the area is generally less crowded. You will have a more comfortable experience, better opportunities to enjoy the views, and more time to take beautiful photos without too many people around.

Overall, the Petronas Twin Towers is not only an architectural masterpiece but also one of the most memorable places to experience when visiting Malaysia.

reviews.author: Andrea Ban
reviews.originalText:
Attended a conference here for the 30th anniversary of MAHTAS and was impressed by the venue overall. Free parking is always a welcome bonus, although I did find the exit a little confusing—the signage could be clearer to guide first-time visitors.

The event space itself was bright and welcoming, with plenty of natural light streaming in through large windows, which gave the place an open, cheerful feel. The air-conditioning was just right—cool enough to stay comfortable without feeling like we were in a freezer.

Lunch was very good, with a nice variety of dishes served promptly and well-presented. The sound system was excellent—clear and well-balanced—and the screen projection was sharp and easy to read from anywhere in the hall. I also appreciated the carpet choice; instead of the usual dark, heavy colours, it was lighter and more pleasant, adding to the fresh, modern feel of the venue.

I had the opportunity to give a talk here, and the audio-visual setup truly did my presentation justice. The layout of the room, seating arrangement, and technical support all worked smoothly, making it an enjoyable experience both as a speaker and as an attendee.

Overall, a well-maintained venue with great natural light, good food, and excellent AV facilities—just needs a bit of improvement in parking exit signage. Would happily return for future events.

reviews.author: Randy Jammy Gabriel
reviews.originalText:
Climbing Mount Kinabalu was truly one of the most unforgettable experiences of my life. From the very beginning of the journey, every moment felt meaningful and rewarding. The cool mountain air, the sound of nature, and the breathtaking scenery created an atmosphere that is both peaceful and inspiring.

The trail itself was challenging, but every step was worth it. Along the way, I was surrounded by lush greenery, unique plant species, and stunning views that made me appreciate the beauty of nature even more. The climb tested my physical strength and mental endurance, but it also taught me patience, determination, and resilience.

Reaching the summit during sunrise was the highlight of the entire journey. Watching the golden light slowly illuminate the vast landscape below was simply magical. It was a moment of pure satisfaction and gratitude, a reminder of how far I had come and what I was capable of achieving.

Beyond the physical adventure, Mount Kinabalu gave me valuable time to reflect, disconnect from daily stress, and reconnect with myself. It was not just a hike, but a personal journey filled with growth, appreciation, and unforgettable memories.

Overall, my experience at Mount Kinabalu was incredible. It is a place that challenges you, rewards you, and leaves a lasting impression on your heart. I would highly recommend it to anyone seeking adventure, self-discovery, and a truly meaningful escape into nature.

reviews.author: Saikhnaa
reviews.originalText: Exceptionally beautiful mountain with incredible surroundings. Desa farm was underwhelming but the ATV ride was a ton of fun especially if you go to the earthquake site.

reviews.author: Celeste Lo
reviews.originalText:
Mt. Kinabalu is more than just a mountain to us locals, she is a huge part of our culture and spiritual life✨. The hike has so many variation of challenges. The humidity, the heat, exhaustion, being wet, cold, climbing in the dark, the altitude, no matter how fit and experienced you are, it is surely an entertaining climb. Most able bodied individuals who are moderately fit will be able to make it to the top, if not, just to Laban Rata is a good achievement as well :)

At the top, the view and the aura is truly amazing. I wish anyone the best as you concur your way to the top, it is absolutely worth it. I will probably do it again, just need to space it out 😅

My guide was the reason I made it to the top, he was so intuitive with the type of support I needed, I couldn’t thank him enough. He was also a great photographer, same caliber as the Bali guides 😂😂

Foreigners are charged differently, locals should not have to pay to same rates. I don’t know where some of the reviewers are getting the confidence to show their entitlement. You do not deserve to pay the same rates, end of story.

The base price includes, the climb, 1 night stay, food, the guide and everything else that makes this climb possible.

First of all, the price to climb our mountain IS expensive because the cost of living and resources in Sabah IS EXPENSIVE. The steps are built and maintained by our people to make it accessible to as many people as possible. There are toilets and rest houses along the way. When you climb the mountain you will see many porters carrying necessities on their backs, up and down so you can have a cup of coffee and sit in a warm room. Thinking you can climb our mountain without our guides is exactly the behavior that will get you lost in this mountain. You will also see many guards and rangers that are there to ensure your safety.

All of this, to make the journey as pleasant as possible and to make sure you get back home to your family safely. Again remember that this mountain is not just a world heritage site for your tourist checklist, many Sabahans including those of older age hike this mountain for spiritual reasons. So how we decide to open our mountain to you, is certainly our choice and you should definitely show some respect.

If not, move along, you do not deserve to climb our beautiful Mount Kinabalu.

reviews.author: Cherry Cheng
reviews.originalText:
This is the biggest climb we’ve done and echoing other reviewers it was very tiring but definitely a memorable, rewarding experience!

We started the hike at Timpohon Gate just before 9am and made it to Panalaban base camp at 330pm. We then began the last leg of the hike at approx 215am and made it to see the sunrise at the summit ☀️ We were super lucky as the sky cleared up for us to see the the incredible view! Before sunrise, we could also see the moon and many stars!!

Coming back was a real struggle for us, as it really put pressure on the legs not to mention it began pouring in our last 3km 🫣 We did finally made it back to the gate just before 4pm - we got a packaged lunch and a van was prepared to take us and other hikers back!

Prior to the hike, we made reservations on their website so the logistics to organise the hike was generally easy and smooth with consistent and efficient communication from staff - both via online leading up to the hike and a day before with reminders for mini van arrangement to and from the hotel. Also, on the van back to the hotel, we dropped a phone, and the driver very kindly pointed it out to us.

We followed their recommended packing list and had everything we needed on the hike. We weren’t too sure about drinking water so we brought extra water (and snacks too!)

Our mountain guide was quite chill but nevertheless, friendly and helpful when we needed him. He helped us navigate the more difficult paths like the rope climbing near the top and he also lent us one of his hiking poles as he noticed one of ours was too short and didn’t help much with stabilising 🫣

reviews.author: Alfred Sun
reviews.originalText:
It's a tough but rewarding experience.
It's probably onevof the most friendly peaks above 4000M accessible to all levels of climbers.
The views from the summit is spectacle, especially if you can make it by the time of sunrise.
The journey from base camp/hut to summit is usually 2.5-3 hrs. The weather can be unpredictable.
A little bit of perseverance, never give up, watch & plan steps ahead,, keep to the pace, stay close to your guide and seek for help whenever needed and that will largely improve success rate.
